reasoning_traces.think:
The core mathematical framework integrates three primary sources of variance in NCAA basketball: location-based performance differences, observer bias in scorekeeping, and referee influence via attendance. These are unified into a multivariate regression model where dependent variables are box score statistics (e.g., FG%, AST, STL), independent variables include game type (home/away/neutral), team strength, and attendance. The model estimates marginal effects of each factor while controlling for others. Dualities emerge in how home advantage manifests differently across genders and divisions, and how observer bias interacts with team strength. Failure modes occur when data lacks sufficient variation in attendance or when neutral games are underrepresented. The kernel of the model is a generalized linear model with logit link function applied to binary outcomes (win/loss) and identity link for continuous box scores.
